title: How long is each side of the regular polygon?
description: A regular polygon with twelve sides has a perimeter of two hundred and eight point eight centimetres. The perimeter is shared by twelve using long division, and the answer is checked by multiplying back.
teaching_notes: One idea: the sides of a regular polygon are equal, so one side is the perimeter divided by the number of sides. Watch for children who lose the point when the ones run out.

source: If the perimeter of a regular polygon with 12 sides is 208.8 cm, what is the length of its side?
video_script.why: The child has divided decimals by counting numbers place by place, and now uses it to find one side of a regular polygon from its perimeter.
video_script.substitution: the book's own regular polygon with twelve sides and a perimeter of two hundred and eight point eight centimetres
video_script.anchor: A regular polygon with twelve sides and a perimeter of two hundred and eight point eight centimetres
video_script.payoff_line: The length of one side is now known.
maths_rules: all 12 sides are equal, so one side = 208.8 ÷ 12
size check: 12 × 10 = 120 and 12 × 20 = 240, so the side lies between 10 and 20
208 Ones ÷ 12: 12 × 17 = 204, so 17 Ones, and 208 − 204 = 4 Ones remain
4 Ones = 40 Tenths, and 40 + 8 = 48 Tenths; 12 × 4 = 48, so 4 Tenths and nothing remains
video_script.design: One idea: one side of a regular polygon is the perimeter divided by the number of sides, worked place by place. Assumes long division of a decimal by a counting number. The polygon stays all video; the side appears only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, divide the same way as the example in your book. All twelve sides are equal, so the perimeter is shared equally.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One side is two hundred and eight point eight divided by twelve.

beats.on_screen: Ones: 208 Ones ÷ 12; 12 × 17 = 204, so 17 Ones; 208 − 204 = 4 Ones remain

marks.m1: two hundred and eight ones are shared by twelve
marks.m2: twelve times seventeen is written as two hundred and four
marks.m3: two hundred and eight take away two hundred and four leaves four ones

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, share the ones. Two hundred and eight ones are shared by twelve.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twelve times seventeen is two hundred and four, so each side gets seventeen ones.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two hundred and eight take away two hundred and four leaves four ones.

beats.on_screen: Tenths: 4 Ones = 40 Tenths; 40 + 8 = 48 Tenths; 12 × 4 = 48, so 4 Tenths; nothing remains

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, change the four ones into forty tenths.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Add the eight tenths that we already have. That makes forty eight tenths.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twelve times four is forty eight, so each side gets four tenths, and nothing is left.

marks.m1: twelve sides of seventeen ones are written as two hundred and four
marks.m2: twelve times four tenths is written as four point eight
marks.m3: the two are added to give the perimeter

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, put the answer back in the question. Twelve times seventeen is two hundred and four.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twelve times four tenths is forty eight tenths, that is four point eight.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Two hundred and four plus four point eight is two hundred and eight point eight, the perimeter.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 17 Ones and 4 Tenths = 17.4; the side is 17.4 cm
